column1: # Unemployment Rate Flow Accounting - Data
# Nicolas Petrosky-Nadeau
# Monthly flows into and out of unemployment
column2: and the unemployment rate they imply:

column1: #   urate            = civilian unemployment rate
#   urate_ss         = steady-state approximation
#   inflow_delta     = inflow rate: entries into unemployment relative to those not
#                      unemployed a month earlier
#   outflow_f        = outflow rate: exits from unemployment relative to those
#                      unemployed a month earlier
#   delta_job_loss   = the E->U (job separation) component of the inflow rate
#   delta_combined   = the remainder of the inflow rate: entry from outside the labor
#                      force plus the labor-force rescaling factor
#   f_job_finding    = the U->E (job finding) component of the outflow rate
#   f_combined       = the remainder of the outflow rate: exit from the labor force plus
#                      the labor-force rescaling factor
# All values in percent. Blank = undefined.
# The flow-based series begin one month after the unemployment rate because they use a
# lagged denominator. October 2025 is blank throughout (the CPS was not collected that
# month); the flow-based series are additionally blank for November 2025.
# Method: Petrosky-Nadeau and Valletta
column3:
#   Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, May 2020, eqs. 3-4 (aggregate rates) and
#   appendix B (components). https://www.frbsf.org/wp-content/uploads/wp2020-18.pdf
#
# Sources: BLS Current Population Survey labor force status flows (LNS17400000,
#          LNS17600000, LNS17100000, LNS17900000) and levels (LNS12000000,
#          LNS13000000), monthly, seasonally adjusted, individuals aged 16 and over.
#
# Suggested citation: Nicolas Petrosky-Nadeau, Unemployment Rate Flow Accounting
